title: Faust, Part One
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
openingText: You've come again, you hovering shapes—I see you now, just as you first appeared to my clouded eyes back then. Should I try, this time, to catch and hold you fast? Does that old illusion still have such a grip on my heart? You're crowding closer now. Then let your reign be granted—sway me out of your misty, shadowy realm! My chest is trembling with a youthful passion, stirred by the magic breezes that rise around your approach.
about: Faust sits up at night surrounded by books. He has studied philosophy, law, medicine and theology and still cannot say what holds the world together at its core. When Mephistopheles appears, Faust risks his life for the chance to feel all that a human being can feel. He meets Margaret, also called Gretchen. Her world comes into focus through a story about her little sister, a song at the spinning wheel and a conversation at the well. Goethe published Part One in 1808.

angleCards.title: What do they wager?
angleCards.text: In heaven Mephistopheles receives permission to try to lead Faust astray. In the study, alone with Faust, he makes a second agreement. Listen for the moment Faust himself sets as the condition.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow the difference between the two wagers.

angleCards.title: What does Margaret know?
angleCards.text: Listen to her questions in the garden. Other people brush aside her uneasiness around Mephistopheles. She keeps taking it seriously.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow what Margaret sees before Faust does.

angleCards.title: When speech turns into song
angleCards.text: The drinkers sing for each other in the cellar. At the spinning wheel Margaret sings alone. What can she say there that she never says to Faust?
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to listen for each song’s audience.

angleCards.title: Who is speaking to whom?
angleCards.text: Two couples pass by in turn in the garden. We hear only a stretch of each conversation at a time. Try reading the four voices aloud.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to read the garden as a scene for four actors.

cast.name: Faust
cast.description: He longs to experience the world he has spent his life studying. In his wager with Mephistopheles he challenges the Devil to satisfy him.

cast.name: Mephistopheles
cast.description: He can be courteous, funny and cruel in the same breath. As Martha’s guest he presents himself as a well-traveled gentleman.

cast.name: Margaret (Gretchen)
cast.description: She keeps house with her mother and helped raise her little sister. Disturbed by Faust’s companion, she asks Faust about his religious beliefs.

cast.name: Wagner
cast.description: When he hears Faust speaking at night, Wagner comes in with his lamp. Their Easter walk brings out their different attitudes to learning.

cast.name: Valentine
cast.description: A soldier, he boasts about his sister’s good name. One night he waits outside her door.

cast.name: The Lord
cast.description: He permits Mephistopheles to put Faust to the test for as long as Faust lives on earth.

whyItMatters.title: Who sets the price?
whyItMatters.body: Faust devises the test himself. If he ever asks a passing moment to stay, the Devil may put him in chains.

whyItMatters.title: A sister and a cradle
whyItMatters.body: In the garden Margaret remembers the nights she spent looking after her little sister. For the first time Faust hears about the work behind her apparently quiet life.

whyItMatters.title: Voices in the dark
whyItMatters.body: In the dungeon a voice can bring hope or terror. Who Margaret thinks she hears changes from one speech to the next.

responses.response: Start in the study. Mephistopheles offers Faust service in this life and asks for the same service in return in the next. Faust answers by making a wager and supplies the words the Devil should listen for. Who will get to decide whether the moment has come?

Try her story about her sister in the garden. She remembers the baby’s weight, the cradle beside the bed and the chores the following morning. What does Faust ask about, and what does she tell him unprompted?
Read the first stanza of the spinning song aloud. Listen for its words again when the stanza returns. What images have come between the repetitions?

preReadingChat.fallback: Choose a short exchange and read it aloud in two voices. Where does one speaker pick up on something the other has said, and where do the two talk past each other?
